title: Anchor Fingers for Fast A-D Chord Changes
summary: JustinGuitar’s lesson centers on the anchor finger technique to speed up chord changes, specifically between D and A chords. The instructor emphasizes keeping fingers light and in position, using the first finger as an anchor while the other fingers lift and reposition, and sliding the anchored finger forward to place the remaining fingers for the A chord. The practice is performed without full pressing or strumming to develop a fluid, rapid transition, with guidance to relax the fingers and avoid tension. The video foreshadows longer-term progression with the concept of 'One Minute Changes' after mastering the anchor approach.

sections.title: What are anchor fingers?
sections.description: Introduces the anchor finger approach: position the D chord with light pressure, keep the first finger as an anchor while lifting the other fingers to form the A chord, slide the first finger slightly, then place the second and third fingers to complete the A. Emphasizes relaxed finger pressure, preparatory positioning without strumming, and a drill-focused pathway to a smooth transition that relies on anchor movement rather than brute finger strength.
